01 Christine Fühlhaber · external expert

To do justice to the project.

An edition project wants to continue. Christine should assess whether his next step is taking. She starts with a simple question.

"How can I live up to the project?"
Explore case ↓Workshop overview
A fictional case story. Persons, projects and sample data are designed for this case. The findings presented are valid within the narrative. This offline unit does not access repositories. Data level of the example: 30 September 2026.

The reviewer and her documentation

A lot of experience, limited time.

Christine loves editions because they make tradition readable and decisions can be discussed. Now, as an external reviewer, she accompanies the next funding decision. She wants to appreciate careful research and at the same time name open questions.

There are proposals, reports and published results. The work programme includes 55 work packages. But what does "finished" mean here?

What she brings

Request for continuationObjectives and resources
Project-reportResults and classification
Edition & PatternSampling

Mission: a reasoned recommendation for the next funding phase, not an automatic funding decision.

Example & Tip: Separate statement and evidence

"42 packages are completed to the verifiable question: Which parts belong to a package, who has professionally released and which version is meant? Christine notes these questions next to the report.

RememberA fair judgement combines scientific results, comprehensible processes and realistic future plans.

Possible next steps
  1. To clarify the mandate and evaluation issues.
  2. Read the report, application and edition together.
  3. Write down open questions on the work programme.

Done if Christine can explain what she is judging and what evidence is missing. Git later helps to compare documented conditions.

For discussion

What information does Christine need first to do justice to the project?

02

Git access / trust through insight

"You can also look under the hood.

The team offers Christine reading rights for an agreed part of the work history. For her this is a positive signal: The project also raises questions that go beyond his report.

It can compare previous file versions and check what was created between two reference days. A nice pattern page gets a temporal connection with it.

"This is an invitation to understand. I don't have to start with a suspicion."

Our proposal: Gradual insight

Project overview→Curated evidence→Reasoned question

Further history becomes accessible specifically and according to agreed purpose. A reading right alone prevents no copies.

Example & Tip: Work repository or publication repositorysitory?

A publication repositorysitory shows verified releases. A working repositorysitory may also contain drafts, rejected solutions and internal comments. One day names a Git-version; it does not yet certify any scientific approval.

RememberTransparency creates a common basis for questions. It is not yet a proof of quality.

Possible next steps
  1. agree on the purpose, scope and duration of the insight.
  2. Provide a designated deadline.
  3. Getting started and contacting us with queries.

Done if Christine finds the relevant version and her contact person. Git helps with named versions and comparisons.

For discussion

What insight would create confidence without revealing more than necessary?

03

File fill / order for outsiders

Many files. A scientific connection.

Leading handwriting, variant, translation, alignment: Four files can be part of a single editorial task. Christine needs a map of the project.

In the example, 220 TEI documents are stored in 55 packages. The team explicitly names contexts instead of letting Christine open them from abbreviations. Open a folder and select a file.

Entry point for the assessment

README.md

The project edifies short narratives. 55 work packages each contain four TEI documents. review-2026-09.

# Erzählräume – Einstieg
1. Arbeitspakete: data/ap-*/README.md
2. Status und Freigaben: docs/freigaben.csv
3. Regeln: schema/edition-v2.sch
4. Beleg für das Gutachten: AP-017

Maintenance: Editorial and technical support update the entry point at each review stand.

The team translates its order

Stable package identifiers connect files, test results and approvals. The README explains for whom the inventory is intended and how to read it.

Example & Tip: Name and Care

ap017_variante-b.xml The identifier remains stable in a new dating. README and share list are maintained with the package; an automatic link test helps against outdated references.

A card is not a total stock

The tree shows a curated section. Other packages and confidential work documents are not included. Previews are synthetic examples.

Example & Tip: Check Work Package

Four existing files do not mean completion. The package also includes documented technical checks and a editorial approval of all agreed layers.

RememberA good README makes a file collection a comprehensible work context.

Possible next steps
  1. Assign files to stable work packages.
  2. Document purpose, roles and status.
  3. Let the entrance of an outsider test.

Done if Christine AP-017 and his approval find out without help. Git also versions these orientation aids.

04

Version history / From difference to question

A reading becomes a reasoned decision.

Christine looks at AP-017 in an exemplary way. Only the story shows her when a documented variant decision was made from an uncertain transcription.

TEI is a XML-based markup for scientific texts. This simplified section shows editorial structures; it is not a complete TEI document.

What can be concluded from this?
Example & Tip: Source and Interpretation

The Diff proves a documented change. The test protocol explains the technical reasons. Commit messages can be scarce, misunderstood or incomplete. Researches, conversations and non-checked intermediates remain invisible. Historical data must be checked with the appropriate rules at that time.

From evidence to overview ↓
Possible next steps
  1. Name earlier and later version.
  2. Separate content change from formatting.
  3. To formulate a technical question for support.

Done if change and justification are separately comprehensible. Git provides the documented states and their difference.

05

Dashboard / overview with way back to the document

"Show me the relevant. And how it comes about."

Christine cannot examine 220 documents individually. She wants a condensed view, whose definitions and limits remain visible.

Interactive demonstrator Git provides file history; status lists and technical tests provide the meaning. This dashboard is a designed prototype, no existing product and no empirical evaluation.

Narrative Spaces · Edition Monitor

Synthetic data

Funding phase 2024–2026 · reference date 30.09.2026 · project-related aggregation

The filter acts on diagnostics, time series and residual work model.

A / Diagnostics

What has been achieved – and how resilient is it?

Work programme and conclusion

Qualified completed / total scope. The intermediate target value comes from the synthetic application.

Quality requires several tests

Technical validity does not replace a scientific quality test. The technical quota refers to documents, the completion to whole packages.

Definition, data base and uncertainty

Final rule v1: all agreed layers available, technical examination passed, editorial review documented, ZX Q1 valid on date. Four documents per package. Synthetic run demo-2026-09-v1, Snapshot review-2026-09. The release list is fully classified; faulty status maintenance is not excluded. No external benchmark available.

The technical sample consists of 12 out of 55 packages (four per type) and is specifically selected and does not allow a statistical extrapolation on the quality of the overall corpus.

Compare exemplary TEI document ↑
Final stability: denominator and follow-up

Substantial reopening requires an earlier approval and a documented new editing problem. Small typing corrections do not count. The eight reopened packages are released again on the deadline. "Stabile- means here only: no documented reopening within six months. Later revisions remain possible.

B / Project dynamics

Disconnect activity, progress and rework.

The curves divide a time axis. Each row is standardized to its own maximum (0–100). The heights compare temporal patterns, no similar amounts. The original values are in the table.

An observation is not yet an explanation. Final sprint, peer review preparation, consolidation and learning can overlap. A change of method can explain an increase; the curve proves no cause.
Original values and measurement rules of the time series

Change event = a commit that affects the selected package type; a commit may be counted multiple times in several types. "All is here the sum of these type events, not a unique commit number. Imports before 2024 are excluded. In the example, closures are package releases adjusted for reopening at the respective quarter end. Reopenings count once each affected package. Basis: synthetic git, issue and release events.

C/Prognosis

What does the next phase need?

The rest has different weights

Planning weights: Key text 1.25; Variants 1.5; Comment-intensive 1.8 units per open package. Weights are assumptions, not measured working hours.

70–130 % of the assumed basic throughput. The controller models capacity for the selected range; it does not evaluate people.

Emphasise scenario

Residual term from October 2026

Bar length = mean residual time relative to the longest scenario in this selection. Specified ranges are assumed planning areas, no statistical confidence intervals.

Model, assumptions and calculation method

Favorable: throughput ×1,25, no additional rework. Middle: basic flow rate, residual circumference ×1,10. Carefully: throughput ×0,8, residual circumferentiality ×1,25. The range ranges from 80 to 130 % of the calculated duration, rounded up to full months. All values are didactic settings, not estimated performance values from Git.

The model makes dependencies, fluctuations and future risks a simple supplement. It has not been validated at later stages. Before real planning it takes capacity commitments, comparison packages, technical complexity testing and a test of previous predictions.

Christine's questions for the report
  • How was the higher complexity of the remaining stock estimated?
  • Which release steps can run in parallel, which depend on each other?
  • Which resources do review and rework actually secure?

Reviewer view: no person profiles, rankings or time patterns. A real implementation requires a coordinated data and access concept.

RememberA good dashboard makes questions based on transparency.

Possible next steps
  1. Agreement on unit, closing rule and benchmark.
  2. Aggregates with verified supporting documents.
  3. Discuss forecasts as conditional scenarios with the team.

Done if Christine can explain any important figure and name its limits. Git provides only a part of the required evidence.

06

Legitimate borders / Christine's responsibility

"Do I need to know that to answer this question?

A file history could lead Christine ever deeper: to individual accounts, times and old notes. But her job concerns the project. She stops.

"I want to understand why a approval takes a long time. I don't need the weekend rhythm of an employee."

A targeted historical comparison can examine an editorial assertion. The meticulous reconstruction of a person's behavior does not automatically answer this technical question.

RememberTechnical visibility does not justify the validity of an evaluation.

What is Christine's question?

Example & Tip: graduated access

Christine starts with project aggregates, then asks for curated document documents and explains a further need. Even small aggregates can make people recognizable. The omission of names alone does not guarantee anonymity.

Committing hours

Offline research, conversations and work before the commit are not fully illustrated.

Example & Tip

A later upload can bundle a whole day of prepared changes. No working time can be derived from this.

Deleted and disappeared

Old file versions can contain internal comments that are missing in the current version.

Example & Tip

An audited document can show a concrete change without passing on the entire internal communication history. A release check must also take into account the included history.

Sharing responsibility

Purpose, access, transfer and storage are institutionally clarified.

Example & Tip

Data protection advice and, where appropriate, interest representation are involved early on. An agreement does not replace any examination of the concrete conditions. This scene is a governance discussion and no legal individual consultation.

Possible next steps
  1. Name the specific assessment question.
  2. Choose the smallest helpful information depth.
  3. To clarify further needs and limits together.

Done if Christine can explain why access is necessary for her question. Git doesn't make a limit enforceable automatically.

For discussion

When would the project review examine individual people?

07

Workshop / Learning from the case together

A fair verdict is teamwork.

Christine needs orientation. The project needs a fair opportunity to classify. Supporters, technology and data protection create the conditions for this.

Our recommended routeClear the evaluation question → read project-related overview → check curated evidence → Commonly classify a query → document limits and assumptions.

Concepts of this case history
Repository: versioned inventory of files. A working repositorysitory contains editing states; a publication repositorysitory offers released results. A collection can connect both functions.
Git History: received file versions and documented changes. It contains traces of the work, not a complete record of the work process. A commit documents a change; a diff shows differences between states.
Test, editorial review and approval: A test examines a finding. A editorial review is a editorial review. A Z XQ2 is a decision about a ZX Q3. Technical validity alone is not a ZXq4.


Basics, implementation and data origin
Conception: previous discussion "Didactic Git Presentation"; provided concept paper "From the Git Repository to the Reasoned Funding Opinion" (22.10.2026); Thomas Jäger, "Edition Practice in the Digital Age: Repositories as Testimonies of Editorial Decision-making Processes?", slides and accompanying script. Design: "Editionskompass · Layout and Design Grundlagen" (Edition Compass), version 1.0.0, and Christine table template.
The slides and the script also open up personal and commit-based analysis models. This prototype follows the project-related assessment specified in the concept paper: qualified approvals, explicit assumptions and data-saving approaches. It does not take over empirical measurement values from the materials.
